# My thinking this year

Alright, let me think about this season. I've got my 3.5 mu like always — wheat in winter, maize in summer. That's what we've been doing for twenty years and it works. My husband and I handle most of the field work ourselves now since two of the kids are working in the city and only come back at harvest to help. The youngest is still in middle school.

On 3.5 mu you can't really get rich, but you can keep the grain bin full and sell a bit for cash. The off-farm money from the kids and from my husband doing some construction work in the slack season — that's what actually pays for things like fertilizer and the children's school. So for the field, I try not to overspend. But I also don't cut corners on the main things, because if the yield drops 100 jin per mu that's real money lost too.

## Wheat

I'll plant around October 10-15, same as always. The agricultural station people say plant by October 15 in our area. I use Jimai 22 — that's what most people around here plant, it resists the cold and stands up well. I buy fresh seed every two or three years from the seed shop, about 40 yuan per mu worth, and keep some of last year's seed for the rest. This year I'm buying new since last year's seed is getting old.

Before planting I put down compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 jin (25 kg) per mu. That's my base. Then at jointing in March-April, if the wheat looks a bit yellow or thin, I topdress urea — about 20-25 jin (10-12 kg) per mu. Altogether that comes out to maybe 16-17 kg of N per mu. The extension fellow says we should target 15 but I like to be a little over, especially on our soil which isn't the best.

For water, I do the winter irrigation in December before it freezes hard — that's important to protect the roots. Then jointing in April, and grain filling in May. So three times. Well water costs about 30 yuan per mu each time through the meter, so that's around 300 yuan total for wheat irrigation on 3.5 mu. I'd skip one if it rained enough, but you can't count on the rain.

I spray herbicide once in early spring for 猪殃殃 and the other weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I'll spray insecticide too. Usually about 30-40 yuan per mu for chemicals.

After maize comes off in September, I do a shallow rotary till and then plant. My husband hires the rotary tiller — we don't own one, not worth it for 3.5 mu.

## Maize

The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is only a few days. I plant right after the combine finishes, usually June 12-18. No time to till — we do no-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble, that's standard now around here. Hire a neighbor's seeder, maybe 15-20 yuan per mu.

I use Zhengdan 958 or sometimes Xianyu 335 — whatever the seed shop has that year that the neighbors say is doing well. Hybrid seed costs about 50 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer on maize, I put the compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 60 jin (30 kg) per mu of compound, plus I topdress urea once at big trumpet stage (about 30-35 jin, 15-17 kg urea per mu). Maize is a greedy crop — it needs more than wheat. Total N comes out to around 14-15 kg per mu.

Irrigation for maize depends on the year. If July-August rain is normal I might only irrigate once at tasseling. If it's dry I'll do two — jointing and filling. Our well is okay but pumping costs add up. Usually I plan for one and hope.

I spray herbicide once after emergence for the grass weeds. Corn borer is the main pest — sometimes I spray, sometimes I don't bother if I don't see much damage.

Harvest in late September-early October. I usually hire a combine — 80 yuan per mu, but it saves us a week of work and the maize doesn't sit in the field getting damp.

## Labor and cash

Mostly just me and my husband. Daughter-in-law helps in the summer when she's home. We don't hire much except the machinery operators. If my husband is away on construction during a busy time, I hire one or two days of help from the village, 150 yuan a day.

For cash — I have about 2000-2500 yuan in hand at the start of the season from last year's maize sale. That has to cover both crops' inputs. If fertilizer prices go up a lot I'll cut back a bit on the topdress. I don't take loans for inputs, I've seen neighbors get stuck that way.

## Yield I'm expecting

If the weather is okay, I expect around 420-450 jin per mu of wheat (210-225 kg/mu... wait, let me think in kg — about 420 kg/mu) and maybe 480-500 kg/mu of maize. That's what I usually get. Last year wheat was a bit lower because of the late spring cold, about 400 kg/mu. Maize was good, 500.
